method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab' (published 31 May 2023). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC10231913). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **NMOSD is a rare, disabling autoimmune disease of the central nervous system**, mainly causing optic neuritis and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis. Prevalence ranges from 0.7 to 10 per 100,000, varying with ethnicity and region, and women are affected more often.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not mistake NMOSD for multiple sclerosis.** It is a separate disease, although the features overlap and misdiagnosis as MS happens.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **About 90% test positive for AQP4-IgG**, a pathogenic circulating antibody and the key diagnostic marker. Lasting problems include loss of vision, weakness, numbness, bladder and bowel problems, nerve pain and fatigue.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treatment has two parts:** managing acute attacks, and maintenance therapy to prevent relapse. Before 2019, all maintenance drugs were off-label: rituximab, azathioprine, mycophenolate, methotrexate, tocilizumab and oral corticosteroids.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eculizumab (a C5 complement inhibitor):** in the PREVENT trial, adjudicated relapse at about 211 weeks was 3% on eculizumab versus 43% on placebo.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Inebilizumab (anti-CD19):** in N-MOmentum, attacks in AQP4-IgG-positive patients were 11% on inebilizumab versus 42% on placebo, over up to 197 days.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Satralizumab (anti-IL-6 receptor), for adults and adolescents 12 and over:** relapse was 11% as add-on versus 43% on placebo (SAkuraSky), and 22% as monotherapy versus 57% on placebo (SAkuraStar).
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Choose on efficacy and safety from trials first**, then relapse severity, the patient's preference for how the drug is given, and comorbidities. How much safety risk the patient accepts also matters.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dosing schedules differ, which shapes preference:** eculizumab is an IV infusion weekly at first then every 2 weeks; inebilizumab is two IV infusions 2 weeks apart, then one every 6 months; satralizumab is a subcutaneous injection every 2 weeks at first, then every 4 weeks.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After a treatment fails, pick one that works differently.** Satralizumab may not help after tocilizumab (both target the IL-6 receptor), and inebilizumab is similar to rituximab (B-cell depletion); consider eculizumab instead.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Leave patients who have no relapses on their present treatment where they are:** the biologic trials excluded stable, non-relapsing patients, so there is no evidence for switching.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With ongoing disease activity on azathioprine or mycophenolate, add more treatment.** About one-third respond poorly to these, especially after severe attacks, and stopping them can raise relapse risk even after 5 years of remission.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Long-term oral steroids** raise infection risk and worsen diabetes, osteoporosis and glaucoma, so moving earlier to a biologic may be appropriate. With a second autoimmune disease, let the more active disease guide the choice.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use the biologic on its own where possible**, because combining it with immunosuppressants may increase infection risk. Clinicians may keep an immunosuppressant (for example, for another autoimmune condition), but should otherwise taper it once the biologic has started.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before switching, allow enough time for the first drug to start working.** The commonest reasons to switch are severe relapse and adverse events. When switching, consider how the previous drug works and how long its effect lasts; trials used 24–48 weeks of follow-up.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Infection is the main long-term safety concern:** watch especially for opportunistic infections, meningococcal meningitis, shingles (herpes zoster) and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. Monitor more closely with infection-risk comorbidities, adolescents, older people, pregnancy and heavy immunosuppression.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bring all vaccines up to date before starting**, not only meningococcal. For eculizumab, labels ask for meningococcal vaccines at least 2 weeks before the first dose, and some countries also require antibiotic cover.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy:** involve a multidisciplinary team. Eculizumab data show no major safety concerns; evidence for inebilizumab and satralizumab is less clear, and inebilizumab in the second or third trimester may cause transient blood abnormalities in the baby.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biomarkers are promising but not yet ready:** a raised serum GFAP predicted attacks and serum NfL after an attack tracked disability in N-MOmentum, but more evidence is needed.
claims.locator: International Delphi panel (23 voting experts), Neurology: Neuroimmunology & Neuroinflammation 10(4):e200124, doi 10.1212/NXI.0000000000200124, 'International Delphi Consensus on the Management of AQP4-IgG+ NMOSD: Recommendations for Eculizumab, Inebilizumab, and Satralizumab', published 31 May 2023, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10231913/, retrieved 2026-09-23
